html:
The first known system of printing with movable type, made in Song China around 1040 by a commoner named Bi Sheng. We know of it only because Shen Kuo described it in his Dream Pool Essays.

Bi Sheng cut single characters into soft clay and baked them hard. To print, he set the pieces in an iron frame coated with a mix of resin, wax and paper ash, warmed it so the type sank into a level bed, then let it cool. Two frames let one page be set while another was printed. Afterwards the type was loosened with heat and sorted for reuse.

The idea did not replace woodblock printing in China, which already turned out huge numbers of books. Chinese writing needs thousands of different characters, so carving a whole page was often just as easy. Later printers tried wood and metal type, and in Korea the Jikji was printed with metal type in 1377. Movable type took off in Europe four centuries after Bi Sheng with Gutenberg, whose alphabet needed only a few dozen letters.
sum: The first known system of printing with movable type, made in Song China around 1040 by a commoner named Bi Sheng. We know of it only because Shen Kuo described it in his Dream Pool Essays.
